newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya to have first S.African-style shopping mall.
newsitem.headline: Kenya to have first S.African-style shopping mall.

text.p: South African developers have unveiled a $60 million plan to open East Africa's first modern shopping centre in the Kenyan capital.
Modelled on South Africa's gleaming shopping malls, construction of "Fox City" on a 30-acre (12-hectare) site on the outskirts of Nairobi will begin next September.

In a brochure released to the press this week, McCormick Property Development (MPD) said the project was the first and the biggest of six planned shopping centres in Kenya and Tanzania with a total lettable area of 117,000 square metres (1.3 million square feet).
Fox City, to be built on what is currently the 20th Century Fox drive-in cinema on Thika Road, will have 125 shops, offices, banks, restaurants and an entertainment centre.

The developers say it will open in October 1998 and are billing it as Africa's largest shopping centre north of the Limpopo, the river marking South Africa's northern border with Zimbabwe and Botswana.

Nairobi's retail sector is dominated by small shops, mostly owned by Kenyans of Indian and Pakistani origin. The city's few supermarkets and shopping malls are crowded and in densely populated areas where access and parking are a headache.
Fox City spokeswoman Diana Bird said MPD executive chairman John McCormick, the developer, was putting funding together with local and foreign investors.
Bird told Reuters major tenants would include Woolworth, Mothercare and British Home Stores.
The entry into shopping centres was the latest proof of South Africa's economic push into the core East African states of Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

So far South African companies have focused on mining, services and breweries. In April South African Breweries Limited announced plans to build a $45 million brewery in Kenya with a consortium of Kenyan entrepreneurs and Dutch development agency DMO.
McCormick and other partners presented the Fox City project to Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi on May 21.
"We went to State House and the president was very keen on Nairobi being a regional centre. He saw Fox City lending an international flavour to Nairobi," Bird said.
Kenyan newspaper reports of the meeting quoted Moi as saying the shopping centre was evidence of strong foreign investor interest in Kenya.
MPD is projecting gross annual sales at Fox City of $150 million and say it will provide 1,250 full-time jobs.
